speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient with a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me the specific name of the antibiotic you took?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Associated Erythema Multiforme. The clinical presentation of an itchy rash starting in the antecubital and popliteal fossae (a "glove and stocking" distribution) spreading to the trunk, combined with fever and joint pain one week after initiating amoxicillin for sinusitis, is characteristic of this drug reaction.
